raw_text:
The method decomposes classification into two complementary parts:  

1. **Global-level recognition:** determine whether the noun phrase/object is present anywhere in the image, \(p(\mathrm{NP\ appears\ in\ image})\). This is predicted using a shared presence token and an MLP classification head. [1]  
2. **Local-level localization:** for each object query, predict the conditional probability that it matches the noun phrase given that the noun phrase is present, \(p(\mathrm{query}_i\mathrm{\ matches\ NP}\mid\mathrm{NP\ appears\ in\ image})\). This component serves as foreground-background segmentation and ranks/localizes the best matching proposal while avoiding duplicate detections. [1,3]  

Thus, the per-query match probability is factorized as  
\[
p(\mathrm{query}_i\mathrm{\ matches\ NP}) =
p(\mathrm{query}_i\mathrm{\ matches\ NP}\mid\mathrm{NP\ appears\ in\ image})
\cdot p(\mathrm{NP\ appears\ in\ image}).
\]
[1]  

At inference, the global presence score is multiplied by each object-query score to obtain the final object score. [3]
